newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Oct 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Oct 29.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- Korean won weakens against dollar, sharply increasing interest payments on foreign debt. The exchange rate has risen by 36 won per dollar during the first half, resulting in foreign exchange valuation loss of about 1.3 trillion won for 538 listed companies.
- Korea's first domestically built 3,200-ton destroyer was launched Monday.
- The U.S. dollar soars to a record high of 843.57 won per dollar on Monday, adding huge foreign exchange loss and foreign debt-servicing burdens to Korean borrowers of foreign currencies.
- About 80 North Korean officers and men were executed by firing squads last year in the wake of a failed military rebellion, a North Korean defector said after arriving in Seoul.
- North Korea's submarine infiltration last month was designed as preparation for war, a captured agent told interrogators.

- The Korean won was down to a record low against the dollar. The Bank of Korea attributed the dollar's hike against the won to a continued weakness of the Japanese yen against the dollar in global markets and a growing demand for the U.S. unit by domestic firms to settle their foreign trade.
- Reiterating his hardline policy toward North Korea, President Kim Young-sam said South Korea will respond with force to the North's provocations.

- Prime Minister Lee Soo-sung reaffirmed that the government would pursue four-nation talks as a viable peace formula on the Korean peninsula, despite the North Korean submarine inclursion last month.
